name: State Machine Example
miniText: What changes when an agent's ongoing behavior is represented as explicit states? NetLogo State Machine Example rewrites the Termites model so each agent stores a task and advances through it under an observer-controlled update. Mealy [1] supplies foundational finite-state machine theory, Dijkstra [2] explains why process ordering matters, and Resnick [3] studies decentralized computational microworlds and the interpretation of collective order. The original Info warns that this version is not behaviorally identical to the turtle-forever-button implementation because the unit of an agent's turn differs. The model therefore illustrates both state decomposition and scheduler semantics. Local chip-handling actions can organize piles without a central plan, but changing execution granularity can change transients. A visually similar final configuration is insufficient to establish equivalent trajectories or a scientifically calibrated model of termite construction.
